messages.author: 580bbc2cd55965b3
messages.subject: Estimators are different in output
parts:
Hi all,

I am testing path analysis with lavaan, and my DV is categorical (0,1).
So I used the WLSMV estimator since I heard that it's reliable.
But the output shows DWLS, though I didn't encounter any error messages.
Do you know why this happens? It seems like sem() automatically adjusts the estimator.


fit <- lavaan::sem(path , data=fit, estimator="WLSMV", bootstrap = 5000)
summary(fit) ## lavaan 0.6.16 ended normally after 238 iterations ## ## Estimator DWLS ## Optimization method NLMINB ## Number of model parameters 76

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: Estimators are different in output
parts:
This is normal. In 'estimator="WLSMV"', the value "WLSMV" is just a shorthand to a set of options. You can take a look at the following threads:

https://groups.google.com/g/lavaan/c/qfCEL5EJlqk/m/AvpiElx4BAAJ

If you use "WLSMV" because you want to handle dichotomous endogenous variables, remember to set the argument "ordered":

https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html

Hope this helps.

-- Shu Fai
